## A common interface

Parsing is separate from feature extraction. The packaged annotations let this
example run without a model download or a new annotation run. Reading native
UDPipe annotations requires the suggested `udpipe` package.

```{r}
library(pseudobibeR.es)
features <- biber(udpipe_samples, measure = "TTR", normalize = FALSE)
features[, c("doc_id", "f_01_past_tense", "f_18_by_passives", "n_tokens")]
audit_features(udpipe_samples, feature = "f_18_by_passives")
```

## Corpus processing

Give each document a unique identifier when annotating. Pass the entire annotated
corpus to `biber()`; one output row is returned per document. UDPipe and spaCy
annotations use the same public interface. Parsing and export remain the
responsibility of the caller.

For spaCy, initialize an installed Spanish model in your chosen Python
environment (for example `r-spacyr`). The following is not run when building
the vignette, because Python and its model are external prerequisites:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
reticulate::use_condaenv("r-spacyr", required = TRUE)
spacyr::spacy_initialize(model = "es_core_news_sm")
parsed <- spacyr::spacy_parse(
  c(doc_1 = "Yo he terminado el informe.", doc_2 = "No vino nadie."),
  dependency = TRUE, tag = TRUE, pos = TRUE, entity = FALSE,
  additional_attributes = "morph"
)
biber(parsed, measure = "TTR", normalize = FALSE)
audit_features(parsed, feature = "f_02_perfect_aspect")
spacyr::spacy_finalize()
```

Morphology must be explicitly requested; the default `spacy_parse()` output
does not supply it. Both native Python morphology objects and serialized
morphology strings are accepted. Optional live tests and frozen annotations
exercise the Spanish spaCy model, but do not establish corpus-level accuracy.

## Interpretation

`normalize = TRUE` divides counts by the document's `n_tokens` and multiplies by
1,000. Function words count in that denominator; punctuation, symbols, spaces,
and UD multiword-token containers do not. `n_lex_tokens` is a separate descriptive
total, not the denominator. The two lexical metrics are not normalized.
Tokenization remains parser-specific: a contraction or enclitic retained as
one spaCy token counts once, whereas supplied UD component words count
separately. The extractor does not infer a missing decomposition.

The usual output has 67 feature columns. `measure = "none"` omits lexical
diversity. Its types are lower-case surface forms with parser tags appended,
not lemmas. Fine-grained tags are retained; missing or `_` tags use UPOS.
Punctuation, symbols, and spaces are excluded by UD POS, and the English
numeric pattern `\d_` removes numeric matches from the tagged stream.
Spelled-out numerals remain words; dictionary expressions are not compounded.

MATTR is the default; if any document has fewer than 200 retained diversity
tokens, the whole supplied corpus uses TTR, with one message. The threshold
population therefore differs from `n_tokens`, which includes number words.
Thus, each document's value is calculated using the same selected measure.
Explicitly selected TTR, CTTR, and MSTTR are retained throughout the corpus.
For MSTTR, `quanteda.textstats` may shorten its common segment length and warns.
Supply the complete corpus together rather than processing documents
independently when relying on automatic fallback. For multivariate analysis,
use the same measure across all compared corpora before scaling.
Documents with no retained diversity tokens receive `NA` for f_43 and an
identifying warning, rather than a fabricated score.

f_28 is zero by compatibility convention, not a measured absence.
`f_59_contractions` counts a bounded inventory of colloquial written reductions,
not ordinary `al/del` or every apostrophe. Surface/span lookup supports `pa`
forms, `onde/nde/onde's/ontas` and reduced `estar` forms despite inconsistent
native tags and lemmas. Each longest recognized expression counts once:
`Ontas? Ven pa’ca’rriba` gives two occurrences. Nominal determiner contexts
and short nominal acronyms are excluded. Supplied annotations and word-token
populations are unchanged, so model-dependent apostrophe/fragment tags can
still affect normalization.

`f_60_that_deletion` is a functional complement-reduction analogue, not only
literal `que` omission. Under the initial creer/pensar/esperar inventory,
infinitival complements (`Pienso ir`, `Creo haber entendido`) and unmarked
finite complements (`Nosotros esperamos lleguen mañana`) count once per
identified clause head. Clear coordinated complements and auxiliary/copular
forms are supported; overt introducers, indirect questions and nominal
infinitives are excluded. `Puedo ir` is not a qualifying lexical complement.
Overlap with f_24 is intentional: infinitive form and complement-reduction
function are different dimensions. This neither reconstructs deletion nor
establishes identical meanings/registers across languages. Supplied annotations
and denominators remain unchanged, and missed predicate/complement analyses
can produce zeros.

`f_62_split_infinitive` measures an adverb interrupting a linked
preposition–verbal-infinitive unit: `Trato de realmente comprender` qualifies,
but `Trato de comprender realmente` does not. Each full matched span counts
once, anchored at the preposition. Consecutive adverbs are supported; subjects,
punctuation and nominal infinitives are excluded. A non-negative adverb is
required: `para no volver` is excluded, but `para no realmente volver` qualifies.
This intentionally differs from negation-inclusive companion heuristics.
Bounded mejor/siquiera lookup and linked auxiliary/copular forms are supported
without rewriting supplied annotations. Missing marker/adverb attachments can
produce zeros; proximity alone is insufficient. f_24 and legitimate f_63
overlap remain independent.

`f_61_stranded_preposition` measures the Spanish resumptive counterpart of
English stranding: `el chico que hablé de él`, competing with pied-piping
`el chico del que hablé`. Initial hablar-de/depender-de/confiar-en frames
require a finite nominal que relative, first/second-person or separate-subject
evidence, and a postverbal linked él/ella/ellos/ellas PP with no known agreement
conflict or bare direct object. `el chico que habló de él` and ordinary object
relatives with unrelated PPs do not qualify. One relative construction counts
once, with its first matching PP span in audits. Detected markers leave the
f_29/f_30 gap bins; pied-piping and other relative bins are unchanged.
Unambiguous hablé/confié lookup handles known native errors without rewriting
annotations. Other frames, gender/coreference ambiguities and model errors
remain outside this bounded baseline. French's f_61 review is recorded but
no companion detector is changed here.
Nominal relatives are partitioned by marker family and role: `que` subject/object
in f_29/f_30, and `quien/cual` forms in f_31/f_32. An article before `que`
does not change its marker family. Pied-piping f_33 takes exclusive precedence;
free relatives, indirect questions and sentential relatives are separate scopes.
Bounded subject-conflict/agreement checks and relative-morphology-based native
attachment recovery do not rewrite input annotations. Roleless `que` needs
positive intransitive/locative predicate evidence or an external subject,
not just absence of another subject. Unresolved gaps can produce zero despite
a genuine relative clause, so parser-based totals are not exhaustive.
The family bins are language-sensitive; pooling f_29+f_31 and f_30+f_32 gives
detected non-pied-piping subject/object relatives, not all relative clauses.
`f_15_gerunds` counts clear noun-like nominal infinitives, such as `el saber`
or `el buen comer`, with nominal internal structure and verified infinitive/verb
identity. Articles alone or bare infinitival subjects are not sufficient.
Qualifying words are excluded from f_14/f_16 noun counts and f_24 verbal
infinitives by occurrence identity; the same shared selection prevents nominal
subjects from licensing impersonal f_09. Noun-tagged forms without infinitive
morphology need a known verb identity, not merely an `-ar/-er/-ir` ending.
Source annotations, word-token populations and lexical metrics are unchanged.
`f_12_proverb_do` counts lexical anaphoric `hacer` with action-proform `lo`
(including enclitics) or `lo mismo`, once on the supplied verb word.
Auxiliary/copular, causative, identifiable reflexive and overt nominal-object
uses are excluded; pronoun/noun counts remain independent of pro-verb counts. Bare `lo hizo`
is a structural candidate, not semantic resolution of a distant antecedent.
`f_09_pronoun_it` counts identified impersonal predicates, not null
pronouns: `Llueve`, `Es importante descansar`, and `Parece que vendrá` each
contribute one occurrence on the existing predicate word. Weather and selected
impersonal clausal rules reject overt nominal subjects and generic personal
pro-drop. Existential `haber` remains in f_20; ambiguous `se` and neuter `lo`
are outside this baseline. Supplied word-token denominators are unchanged;
UD empty nodes are not counted.
Language-specific constructions, parser errors, and lexical inventories mean
that identical column names do not guarantee cross-language equivalence.
Do not interpret scores against English factor norms as validated Spanish scores.

## Auditing

Use a canonical feature identifier or category letter. Each audit row identifies
one token or multiword construction; raw document counts can be recovered by
summing the `count` column within a document and feature.

```{r}
audit_features(udpipe_samples, category = "A", sample_n = 3, seed = 42)
```
